items.title: Binance reopens withdrawals in phases, starting with bitcoin
items.why: New today: Binance began restarting withdrawals for bitcoin, ether, USDT, USDC, BNB and XRP and says it has replaced about 95% of the $6.3 billion stolen. Analysts tie the hack to North Korea's TraderTraitor group.
items.action: Move crypto you hold for the business to a wallet you control, and keep exchange balances to what you need for day-to-day trading.

items.title: Drupal Commerce flaw is being exploited against online stores
items.why: Drupal says attackers are abusing a missing-permission bug in Commerce Core, the module behind carts and checkout, and warns it can cost store owners money. Fixed releases are out.
items.action: Update Drupal Commerce Core to 3.3.13 (or 8.x-2.41 on older sites) today, then review recent orders and refunds for anything odd.

items.title: Fake IT help desk on Microsoft Teams led to full domain takeover
items.why: Microsoft says attackers posing as IT support on Teams talked staff into opening Quick Assist, then abused weak certificate settings to take over admin accounts and copy files out.
items.action: Block or limit Teams chats from outside companies, and tell staff IT will never ask them to start Quick Assist on an unexpected call.

items.title: CISA adds two more Ivanti VPN flaws to its exploited list
items.why: Update: CISA now lists two more Ivanti Connect Secure bugs used in the same attack chain as known exploited, with a federal fix deadline of November 2.
items.action: Upgrade Ivanti Connect Secure to 25.1.1.3 or 22.8R2.6 now and check the appliance for signs of earlier compromise.

items.title: Fake Claude Code extension on Cursor tried to plant a backdoor
items.why: For about 11 hours on October 29, two tampered versions of the Claude Code extension on Cursor's marketplace tried to add an attacker's SSH key and a startup task on developer machines.
items.action: Check developer machines for Claude Code extension versions 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 from Cursor; if found, remove unknown SSH keys and startup entries.

items.title: MDaemon mail servers hacked through a booby-trapped attachment
items.why: ESET found attackers emailing a malicious RAR file to MDaemon servers; the built-in virus scanner opened it and planted malware with no one clicking anything. MDaemon 26.0.4 fixes it.
items.action: Update MDaemon to 26.0.4 or later, and confirm its bundled antivirus engine is current.
